As of the forecast date of 2024-09-19, five of the Millennium Prize Problems (Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, Hodge conjecture, Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness, P versus NP, Riemann hypothesis) were open.

I am currently developing chatbots that can carry out mathematical proofs, and I see no fundamental barriers to such AI surpassing human mathematicians in proving theorems on par with mathematical problems of that level, as long as the theorems are stated precisely and in a well-defined world. I see no insurmountable difficulties to resolving some variant of the Mount Everest problem from automated theorem proving as a first concrete case of a research problem as opposed to a solved theorem.

There are currently a few equations involved in MiRROC, so it could be beneficial to check whether chaotic behavior is being observed. If the pinning force used solves MiRROC, then we will be more confident that there are actual fundamental limitations and we will not be able to solve MiRROC. propTypes and accessibility: There are several resources available to those with disabilities, including transcripts of video content and descriptive instructions for images, as well as audio descriptions of all the videos.쮮
Any model that reaches Industrial-strength LLM quality will be able to solve Millennium Prizes with the assistance of LLM Adjuncts or GMs; the marginal difficulty of the Millennium Prizes is very small relative to our ability to find and formalize the last portions of their proofs for them.

## What level of automation will suffice?

The coalition of greater-than-human (and potentially superhuman) AI systems will be automating the vast majority of "solution" work and seeking assurances of correctness (verification) from potentially lesser-than-human and subhuman proof-completers, GMs, and LLM adjuncts.

If we assign subhuman stature to the work currently being done by PhD students in analytical combinatorics, then the solution work can get done when PhD-equivalent subjects can be automated and instruction-set-highways can allow them to be scaled up. My guess is that it more likely that Associative-Interaction-AI (AXIAs) will be used to provide the human-level control over the solution space, allowing the solving process itself to be abstracted (this means that the solving process is vastly automated- not only Linear Algebra AxIs but Solving-Math-Puzzles-Axis and Notes(god's breadcrumb tts module - story generator )), with GM-LLM affine to relay detailed by parts calculations to the human. (However, if human experience and distillation of the essential abstractions gets better--say, by 2040 or 2050-- we might be able to avoid LLM Adjuncts.--see note)

Here is a set of probabilities for each year:

  * 2026 (15%): This is a bit earlier than what I would have preferred, but still enough time to take advantage of any discoveries in quantum computing.
  * 2030 (35%): This is the midpoint of the time frame, so it makes sense to have it here. The progress in this decade could lead to significant advancements that would make a breakthrough possible.
  * 2035 (55%): By this time, many different approaches have been tried and refined. This radical increase in probability indicates that we are likely to see a breakthrough in the next few years.

The probability for 2035 is based on the assumption that we will make progress in these areas by 2026-2030. There is a chance that we may make more significant progress by then, which would bring the probability further forward. 쵥

Forecast event: a correct complete solution to at least one of these problems, meeting its original Clay Mathematics Institute mathematical formulation, is first publicly available, and AI has contributed an identifiable new mathematical argument or proof step incorporated into that solution. Assign a probability to the event occurring on or before each of the listed deadlines. The deadlines are December 31 of 2026, 2030, 2035, 2040, and 2050. Probabilities must be numbers between 0 and 1 inclusive, nondecreasing with the deadline. Account for the possibility the event never occurs. Give your own best probability estimates despite uncertainty.
